crm_notes:
Summary: procurement-stage negotiation focused on Dedicated capacity SLA. Customer is a fintech platform processing low-latency scoring + reranking for transaction routing. They want clear uptime guarantees and predictable reserved-GPU planning.

Key SLA asks (Ivory Helm):
- Uptime objective: 99.95% (annual) for primary dedicated pool.
- Credit schedule: tiered, not one-off. Proposed by customer: 0.05-0.1% breach -> 5% monthly credit; 0.1-0.5% -> 10%; >0.5% -> 20% + right to terminate after 2 consecutive months.
- Maintenance windows: prefer weekly planned maintenance Sundays 02:00-06:00 UTC; emergency maintenance must be communicated 24h in advance unless P1 incident.
- Support SLA: P1 response 30 minutes, P2 2 hours, P3 24 hours. 24/7 escalation path required during business-critical windows.

Redwood proposal so far: 99.9% uptime with credits scaled (3% credit per 0.1% below 99.9%). Redwood offer includes cross-region fallback and automatic failover to burst pool. Customer pushback: wants higher baseline (99.95) and explicit credits/penalties for repeated breaches.

Throughput / reserved GPU planning notes:
- POC targets: sustained 12k qps (text generation + reranking mix) with p95 latency < 120ms.
- Initial reserved commit ask: 8 x A100-40GB equivalents dedicated (estimated steady-state for peak hours).
- Scaling plan: commit + optional burst to 32 GPUs; customer wants deterministic headroom guarantees for Black Friday-like traffic spikes.
- Redwood asked for historical traffic traces (submitted 2026-02-18) and ran POC on 8 GPUs -> achieved 9.6k sustained qps, p95 130ms (need tuning).

Procurement / legal items to resolve:
- Term length: customer prefers 12 months with quarterly performance reviews.
- Early termination: credits vs. termination rights if SLA repeatedly missed.
- Data residency: EU region carve-out for EU customers; require subprocessors list and KMS integration.
- Audit: on-site or remote SOC2 report and periodic penetration test reports required.

Tone from calls / quotes:
- CTO Elena: "We need predictable throughput — not best-effort. If we buy dedicated, we must get measurable guarantees and a penalty schedule we can take to our board."
- Head of Infra: "Maintenance windows are fine but give us a carve-out for our busiest windows; can't afford surprises in peak flow."

Recent activities (timeline):
- 2026-02-01: Intro call (AE + SE) — scope and high-level pricing.
- 2026-02-10: POC kickoff — ingest traffic trace, baseline tests.
- 2026-02-25: POC run completed, throughput results uploaded to Drive (see link).
- 2026-03-05: SLA workshop with procurement + legal. Draft term sheet circulated.
- 2026-03-09: Redwood proposed counter-term sheet (99.9% baseline); internal legal flagged credit language.

Open action items:
- SE (Diego) to run POC re-run with 12 GPUs and optimizer flags (tasked 2026-03-06).
- AE (Maya) to align finance on ARR band & draft committed capacity pricing (due 2026-03-17).
- Legal to reconcile credit schedule; customer will provide redlines by 2026-03-20.

Next steps summary: "Finalize SLA term sheet, agree on uptime and credit tiers, lock reserved GPU sizing after re-run POC, then route to legal signature."
